reply.subject: RM_UniversalPipe_Scrapper

observed.facings.png: A 4x4 linked-pipe atlas on a checker background, labelled 'south'. It holds straights, quarter elbows, tees, a cross, end caps and an isolated single cell. The pipe is a thin, dark-outlined tube in oxidised copper with sparse teal verdigris flecks. Tees and crosses carry a round domed boss with small rivets around its rim. Dead ends finish in a rounded cap with a dark banded collar. The elbows are smooth arcs that run along the pipe axis. The isolated cell is a single riveted boss.
observed.south.png: The same atlas on real alpha with no background. The edges are clean and there is no shadow or halo. The tube has the same width and colour band in every tile. The bosses are centred on the junctions. The end-cap collars look like a few wraps of dark wire or band.
observed.single.png: Identical to south.png: the same atlas on real alpha.
observed.scale.png: An offline render at 96 px/cell on a dirt-brown ground. It shows a long horizontal run with an end cap at the left, a valve near the left, a tee with a riveted boss and a short vertical branch ending in a capped end, a sprinkler head mid-run, and an S-shaped pair of elbows rising to an upper run that ends in a cap. A vanilla pawn stands beside it in a panel at the right. The pipe is thin and flat next to the pawn. Joins between cells are seamless. Small teal flecks repeat along the runs at roughly regular spacing.
observed.siblings.png: Reference only: the checker area is empty, and below it is the industrial sibling rendered on the same layout. That sibling is a thinner grey-steel pipe with small dark fittings.
observed.assembled_1.png: The same layout at 90 px/cell. The runs are continuous and the elbows join the straights cleanly on the axis. The tee boss sits on the junction centre. The valve and sprinkler draw on top of the pipe. Each end cap closes its run with a collar. The teal flecks recur at a visible per-cell interval along the long horizontal run.
observed.assembled_2.png: The same layout at 48 px/cell. It still reads clearly as a copper pipe with a tee, an S-bend and caps. The boss shows as a small knot at the tee and the caps as small dark nubs. The verdigris is barely visible, so the pipe reads mostly as plain copper.

CAMERA.seen: A floor pipe drawn flat by Graphic_Linked. The card's engine limits say pipe is flat ground art seen top-down, so the 35-degree building camera does not apply. The bosses and caps are domed and lit consistently.

BORE.seen: No open bore appears anywhere. Every dead end is closed by a cap, and the isolated cell is a closed boss.

PORTS.seen: In assembled_1 and assembled_2, every straight, elbow and tee meets its neighbour at the cell edge on the same axis and width with no gap or offset. The valve and sprinkler sit on the run.

PORTS_DRAWN.seen: Each tile's pipe ends reach the edges where the mask has neighbours. There are no stray connectors and no stubs where no neighbour exists; dead ends carry caps.

LAYERS.seen: The valve and sprinkler head draw over the pipe, and the tee boss draws over both pipe arms.

ROTATIONS.seen: There is one atlas. Every tile uses the same tube width, palette, boss and cap design. The vertical and horizontal caps match.

SIGNATURE.seen: Present: an oxidised copper tube, elbows with a half-cell radius on the axis, riveted scrap-plate bosses at the 3- and 4-way junctions, and wire-wrapped collar caps on dead ends. The 'mismatched iron and brass fasteners' read only as uniform small rivets at normal zoom, so the scrap/salvage character is mild.

MATERIAL.seen: The tube reads as dark copper metal: it has cylindrical shading with a lit centre line and dark edges, and the verdigris flecks read as oxidation, not paint.

FOOTPRINT.seen: The tube is thin, centred in each cell and stays inside the linked cells. The bosses are slightly wider than the tube but stay inside the cell.

ALPHA.seen: Clean cut-out in south.png, with no ground patch, shadow or halo. The code also measures real alpha as present.

OURS.seen: Bespoke copper strip, bosses and caps. They do not match vanilla or any known mod pipe art.

OWNER_NOTES.seen: The alignment defects behind 'bad art alignment' are visibly fixed: the elbows sit on the axis, the tee boss is centred, the caps are attached and there are no padding seams. Whether the art is 'still bad' is a matter of taste. It is now coherent, but it reads as tidy steampunk copper rather than junk-built.

LEGIBLE.seen: At 48 px/cell (assembled_2) the run, tee, S-bend and caps are all clear. At 32 px it will read as a thin copper line, which is appropriate for floor clutter.

reply.subject: RM_UniversalPipe_Scrapper
reply.image_seen: Image 1 shows a copper pipe atlas on checkerboard; images 2–3 show the same atlas on black; image 4 shows an assembled run beside a pawn; image 5 shows the industrial sibling; images 6–7 show offline assemblies at different scales. No in-game capture is supplied.

concerns.evidence: Images 2–3 show dark, mottled copper with green oxidation, uneven surface marks, darker collars and contrasting light and dark fasteners around the bosses. The assembled runs retain a weathered material appearance. The bosses are regular and symmetric, but the description explicitly requests round symmetric bosses; that regularity alone does not establish a missing salvage identity.

The long horizontal run in image 6 has recurring bright copper and teal marks at regular intervals. The rhythm is faint, with continuous pipe width and no obvious detached sections or elbow kinks. Repetition itself follows the stated Graphic_Linked limitation; the remaining concern is the prominence of the repeated surface marks.

Images 4 and 6 show continuous straight runs, smooth elbow transitions, an axis-centred junction and attached end caps. Images 2–3 also show oxidation and darkened fittings. These visibly address the owner's alignment and art complaint; 'modest charm' does not establish that the note was ignored.

The images show flat ground pipes, consistent with the card's explicit engine limit: 'pipe is flat ground art seen top-down; no height or shadow is drawn by the engine'. The generic elevated-building camera requirement therefore does not justify a camera failure here. Separately, the supplied assemblies are explicitly offline renders, so the class module's required running-game verification remains unavailable.

edits.change: The straight strip's verdigris is a very fine, low-contrast grain, evenly scattered at the same small scale and the same muted tone everywhere in the cell, with no isolated bright teal spots, so a run of repeated cells reads as one continuous weathered tube.

The straight texture carries only low-contrast oxidation flecks spread uniformly across its seamless, non-mirrored cell period, with the copper highlights and the teal tones both damped to a narrow value range, so repeated cells read as continuous weathered copper.

invariants: One oxidised, darkened copper tube of uniform width and colour band, identical along every cell
Seamless non-mirrored single-cell period on the straights, with left and right edges matching exactly
Elbows bent on the pipe axis with radius of half a cell
Round symmetric boss of scrap plate with mismatched iron and brass fasteners at every 3- and 4-way junction
End cap with a crude wire-wrapped solder collar on dead ends
Pipe drawn flat, low and thin: 18 px of a 132 px cell, ground clutter under pawns

Fine dents and the salvage character kept in the fittings and the overall oxidation, not in per-cell one-off marks
request.prompt: RimWorld floor pipe for water, Scrapper (salvage, junk-built) look, painterly vanilla RimWorld style, realistic, clean dark outline, transparent background, seen from directly above as flat low ground clutter under pawns. Linked 4x4 atlas for Graphic_Linked, 132 px cells, tube 18 px thick, centred on the cell axis. Straight runs: one oxidised, darkened copper tube of uniform width and a single uniform colour band, the same along every cell. The tube surface is a very fine, low-contrast verdigris grain, evenly scattered at the same small scale and in the same muted dark-teal-green tone over the whole cell, with copper highlights and teal tones both held to a narrow value range; the surface has soft shallow dents and no isolated bright teal spots and no bright copper glints, so repeated cells read as one continuous weathered tube. The straight is cut as a single seamless, non-mirrored cell period whose left and right edges match exactly, with the oxidation texture distributed evenly across the full cell length and no feature concentrated at one position in the cell. Elbows are bent on the pipe axis with a radius of half a cell, the same tube width, colour and grain as the straights, so they join the straights with no kink. Tees and crosses: a round symmetric boss of scrap plate centred on the junction, with mismatched iron and brass fasteners, the pipe arms meeting it on the axis. Dead ends: the tube ends in a cap with a crude wire-wrapped solder collar, attached flush to the tube end. All tiles share the same copper colour, grain scale and outline weight, so the atlas assembles into a straight run with a tee, an elbow pair and three end caps that join up seamlessly.
